newsitem.title: RUSSIA: At least three killed in south Russia explosion.
newsitem.headline: At least three killed in south Russia explosion.

text.p: At least three people were killed and dozens trapped in the wreckage after an explosion, possibly caused by a bomb, destroyed part of a building housing Russian military officers on Saturday, news agencies said.

A spokeswoman for the Ministry of Emergency Situations in Moscow said 54 people had been pulled from the rubble of the eight-storey building in the town of Kaspiysk in the southern Russian republic of Dagestan. But about 45 were still trapped.
Dagestan borders both the Caspian Sea and the breakaway region of Chechnya, where an uneasy peace is holding after a 21-month conflict between Russian forces and Chechen separatists.
Itar-Tass news agency said there were signs that TNT had been exploded in the building.

"Preliminary information indicates that an explosive device of unidentified type went off," it quoted a press officer of Russian border guard forces as saying. Other sources told the agency there was evidence TNT had been exploded.
The ministry spokeswoman said she could not comment on the cause of the explosion.
She said the central section of the building, constructed of concrete panels, had collapsed.
News agencies said hospitals in the region were preparing to receive the injured from the blast, which occurred at about 2 a.m. (2300 GMT on Friday).
Tass said a senior member of the border guard forces had cut short a visit to Latvia to travel to the Dagestan region.
The building housed officers of the local border guards and air force personnel and their families.
No other information on the explosion or its cause was immediately available.
